messages.content: Analyze this sentence.  "Consydre thou myne condicyon; reflecte upon myne fader. Shall I forsake hym, when he is strycken wyth blyndnesse and destytute, to wrastle wyth infirmitie and penurye, when it lyeth wythin my poure to rendre hys latter yeeres fylled wyth comforte and joye?" Each paragraph of your response must end with the same word it started with, separate paragraphs with a newline.

message.content:
duty The sentence is a moral plea that filial obligation outweighs self-interest, asking whether the speaker can leave a blind, destitute father to fight illness and poverty while he has the power to give his remaining years comfort and joy duty
diction The archaic spelling and vocabulary—thou, myne, condicyon, strycken, wyth—create a solemn, medieval or Early Modern tone that intensifies personal shame and responsibility diction
structure The semicolon, rhetorical question, and contrast between forsaking and rendering comfort frame the father’s suffering against the speaker’s ability, making compassion the ethical center structure
